en: The Philippine flag features a sun with exactly eight rays, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippines consists of 7,641 islands, which is over 500 more than the previously officially counted 7,107 islands.
The Philippine Senate has 24 members, whereas the House of Representatives has over 300 members representing various districts and sectors.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but the 1987 Constitution designates only Filipino and English as the two official languages.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote exactly two major novels, Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, before his execution at age 35.
Cebu's famous Sinulog Festival features a nine-day celebration that always culminates on the third Sunday of January.
The Cordillera Administrative Region in Luzon is home to at least 18 distinct ethnolinguistic indigenous groups, including the Ifugao and Kalinga.
Dr. Fe del Mundo became the first female student at Harvard Medical School in 1936 and later founded the country's first pediatric hospital.
The current 1987 Constitution of the Philippines contains exactly 18 articles that define the powers and limits of the three government branches.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva created over 100 sculptures during his lifetime, earning him the title of Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture.
The secret society Katipunan grew rapidly from just seven original founders in 1892 to over 30,000 members by the 1896 revolution.
The Philippines celebrated its 100th year of independence from Spain in 1998, exactly a century after the 1898 proclamation in Kawit, Cavite.
